name: robot_localization extended Kalman filter implementation
summary: Official C++ Ekf library implementation for selective measurement correction and nonlinear state/covariance prediction in robot_localization. This source mutates filter state and covariance; it is not a standalone ROS node, sensor-interface implementation or verified localization task.

license.scope: Selected src/ekf.cpp has a complete BSD-3-Clause notice, copyright 2014-2016 Charles River Analytics, Inc. and 2017 Locus Robotics, Inc. Preserve its copyright, conditions, disclaimer and non-endorsement requirement. Root LICENSE includes Charles River Analytics and Austin Robot Technology BSD notices, with an organization placeholder in one clause; package.xml instead declares Apache License 2.0. Verification is limited to the explicit, complete selected-file notice. It does not relicense or clear the full package, other components, dependencies or binaries.

packages: Complete pinned robot_localization package, rl_lib, headers and FilterBase/Measurement implementations
system: Caller-provided initialized filter state, covariance, measurement/update masks and process/control settings
Consistent units, frames, measurement timing and rclcpp Time/Duration values
C++ toolchain and generated package interfaces required by the reviewed CMake configuration
requirements.notes: correct selects finite measured dimensions, takes the absolute value of negative covariance diagonals, floors very small diagonal variances at 1e-9, computes a Kalman gain by matrix inversion, normalizes angular innovation, applies a Mahalanobis threshold and updates state/covariance using the Joseph form. predict builds an Euler-angle transfer function and analytical Jacobian, calls inherited control preparation, optionally computes dynamic process noise, projects state/covariance and wraps state angles. It uses 1/cos(pitch); numerical conditioning and singularity behavior were not tested. These methods mutate filter internals and can emit configured debug output; this file defines no main, ROS subscriptions/publishers or physical robot command. CMake places src/ekf.cpp in rl_lib and separately builds ekf_node from another source that was not read in this bounded review. CMake selects C++17 for non-WIN32 builds. Package version 3.8.3 and ROS Index jazzy-devel metadata are declarations, not tested ROS, OS, architecture, Python or sensor compatibility. A fetched file alone is insufficient.

invocation.notes: Library methods, not a shell command or standalone source-file executable. The selected file defines predict(const rclcpp::Time &, const rclcpp::Duration &) and correct(const Measurement &). Its complete package supplies class declarations, inherited filter state/utilities and caller integration. Reviewed CMake links rl_lib into a separate ekf_node target, but that target main and ROS filter I/O were not reviewed here. No Hub build, install or execution adapter is provided; no upstream library, ROS node, simulator or robot was compiled, loaded or run.

access.instructions: Read the selected implementation, complete per-file notice, package declarations and CMake configuration before integrating the full upstream library. This source reference only retrieves one inert file; it does not provide a prepared sensor-fusion node or run a localization task.

Complete EKF implementation, root license, package XML and CMake read as inert text; all four immutable file bodies matched tree Git blobs and sizes. Library entrypoints, mutation boundaries, declared dependencies and BSD-file/Apache-package distinction inspected. No compiler, imports, installation, ROS execution, sensor data, numerical test or physical compatibility verification.
